office.remit: Mayor-council city of more than 12,000 people under Alabama general law (Title 11, Chapter 43). The mayor is the chief executive officer: supervises departments (Administration, City Clerk, Accounting and utility billing, Engineering, Street, Sanitation, Water/Sewer, Building Inspections, Parks and Recreation, Police, Fire Rescue, Municipal Court), signs contracts and is not a voting member of the council. The five-member City Council (elected at large by place) passes ordinances and resolutions, awards bids, approves land purchases and adopts the budget; it elects its own president and president pro tempore (Ala. Code 11-43-2). The appointed City Clerk keeps council records, business licenses and cemetery records. Fiscal year Oct 1 - Sept 30; the FY2027 budget was adopted Sept 14, 2026. Community storm shelters are listed and activated by Cullman County EMA; the city owns the shelters on city property. Elections are nonpartisan (August, every four years).

succession.rule: Ala. Code 11-43-42: in a city of 12,000 or more inhabitants, 'in the event of a vacancy from any cause in the office of mayor, the president of the council shall succeed to the office of mayor for the unexpired term'; the president's council seat is vacated (Alabama League of Municipalities, Handbook for Mayors and Councilmembers 2025, sec. 18(b)). The council elects its president from its members (Ala. Code 11-43-2) and may remove its president and elect another at any time (AGO 1992-0145, cited in the League handbook). A vacancy in the council presidency is filled by the president pro tempore (11-43-42); a council seat vacancy is filled by the council at a regular meeting after the one at which the vacancy is declared (Ala. Code 11-43-41). Cullman's population (about 18,200 in 2020) puts it in the 12,000-and-over rule. The previous mayor's term (2025-2029) ends in November 2029; the next municipal election is the fourth Tuesday in August 2029.
succession.how_the_council_chose_her: The roster route ('chosen by the city council to fill the remainder of the term') is realized the only lawful way for a city of Cullman's size: the council chose who would succeed by choosing its president. On Sept 14 the sitting council president (Place 5) gave up the presidency, saying he would not leave his seat and business to serve as mayor, and the council elected Denise Kreuzer (Place 3) president, 4-0 with Kreuzer abstaining, knowing the president would succeed when the resignation took effect on Sept 18.
succession.timeline: Wed Sept 2: previous mayor delivers a written resignation to the City Clerk, effective 5:00 p.m. Fri Sept 18 (no reason given anywhere on the drive). Mon Sept 14: council meeting; Place 5 resigns the presidency; council elects Kreuzer president; FY2027 budget adopted. Fri Sept 18, 5:00 p.m.: resignation effective; Kreuzer succeeds to mayor; her Place 3 seat is vacated. Mon Sept 21, 9:00 a.m.: oath and ceremony, City Hall auditorium. Mon Sept 28: council president pro tem (Place 2) becomes council president by statute; council elects Place 4 as pro tem; Place 3 vacancy declared, applications to Oct 7. Mon Oct 12: council appoints Dwayne Pickard to Place 3.

how_the_office_works.staffing: The mayor's office is part of Administration: the mayor, an executive assistant, and a Director of Communications who also serves as the mayor's chief of staff (Cullman has a City Communications office; the chief-of-staff role is this office's invention). Staff are city employees paid from the General Fund.
how_the_office_works.approvals: City Council awards bids, approves land purchases, adopts the budget, and appoints to fill council vacancies; the mayor presents items and executes contracts but does not vote. Special-event permits are issued by the City Clerk; police details for events are billed by the Police Department under the city's special events policy. Cemetery spaces are sold by the City Clerk's office; the sexton (Street Department) marks graves.
how_the_office_works.routing: Threats, legal action and media go to Bryce Templeton (Director of Communications and Chief of Staff).
